payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear comparison of segmentation performance between words and morphemes, indicating that morpheme-based references yield better metrics in unsupervised settings, while word-based references perform better with word supervision.

claims.text: Segmentation metrics are better with morpheme-based references in unsupervised settings, indicating morphemes may provide more accurate segmentation.
With word supervision, word-level metrics improve, while morpheme boundaries do not match this improvement, suggesting a trade-off in performance based on the type of supervision used.
The results suggest that using morphemes can lead to oversegmentation, while words can be undersegmented, highlighting the complexity of segmentation tasks.
